scope: Read-only attribution and proposed next test; no new experiment authorization, implementation, execution, or savings claim.

measurement.author: root-run physical Cinnamon X11 diagnostic; inspected saved output only

attribution.claim: The app deliberately retains each lazily constructed QWidget and its child graph after close/hide; drafts, selections, model state and live signal connections survive. Actual widget deletion occurs at owner teardown. Settings Cancel is a separate intentional discard path.

Close already destroys the native QWindow platform surface. Its PlatformSurface event uses QWidget::destroy(false,false), retaining top-level backing-store ownership. Hide similarly unmaps without freeing the store. Reopening reuses that store. Changing native XIDs in the receipt agrees with this lifecycle. Calling only windowHandle()->destroy() would repeat an existing step.

All three views start at 1000x700. Three 32-bit raster buffers, each page-rounded to 2801664 bytes, total exactly 8404992 bytes, matching the observed memfd:xorg RSS. Qt Xcb obtains its shared segment from Xorg, mmaps it, and holds it with the backing-store image. This strongly attributes the retained mapping to these three raster stores, although no per-object addresses or runtime sizes were measured.
attribution.confidence: strong source-and-size inference; not object-level runtime proof

attribution.claim: The empty diagnostic has zero operations. History already cancels pending preview work and clears its pixmap on hide, so a retained user thumbnail is not an explanation for this empty-view mapping.

The +12435456-byte heap RSS is an arena mapping footprint, not a live-allocation counter. Retained widget/text/layout/style state is live; freed arena pages and fragmentation may also contribute. The saved result cannot partition them. malloc_trim cannot release live raster stores or widget state. Native font and clean code mappings account for much of the remaining increase and should stay.

preferredNextTest.operation: From each existing top-level QWidget subclass, defer the documented protected QWidget::destroy(true,true) until the close/hide event stack has returned; recheck that the same widget is still explicitly hidden and alive before releasing native resources.
preferredNextTest.why: Small resource-lifecycle change with no draft serialization, child-widget deletion, or new allocator policy. Qt6.4.2 deleteTLSysExtra clears the repaint manager, deletes QBackingStore (which deletes the Xcb image/SHM/pixmap), then destroys the QWidgetWindow. Logical widgets and their settings/history/activity state remain. Normal show creates a new native window/backing store and invalidates the full view for repaint.
preferredNextTest.timing: Use a QObject-context deferred callback or equivalent lifetime guard; do not destroy the QWidgetWindow synchronously inside its current close/hide dispatch. Skip if reopened before the callback. A minimize-generated spontaneous hide leaves isVisible true and must not release the minimized view.
preservationChecks: WM close and explicit hide both preserve unsaved synthetic settings draft/conflict state, selected section/profile, geometry and controls; explicit Cancel continues its existing discard behavior.
History selected rows/filter/scroll and active deletion-cancel control survive; preview remains cleared while hidden and reloads on show. Activity selection and result actions still work.

Rapid hide/show, repeated three-view cycles, minimize/restore, shutdown with queued release, and native file/help dialogs produce complete repaint without stale pointers, warnings or changed fonts/theme.
Existing GUI source tests already cover preview release/reload and active deletion cancellation across hide/show; add focused resource-release coverage only if a new experiment is authorized.
preferredNextTest.measurementProposal: Root alone repeats the existing physical three-view observer on a separately authorized candidate. Compare memfd:xorg RSS/PSS, total RSS/PSS/private, first reopen latency and complete next-show paint. Observe backingStore/windowHandle null after deferred QWidget release and fresh nonzero size after show using a bounded synthetic diagnostic. If heap remains large, separately record allocated versus free arena bytes before/after release to locate live widget costs; do not infer them from heap RSS. Keep any allocator policy unchanged in the first probe.
preferredNextTest.expectedDirection: Source predicts release of these live raster mappings while hidden; actual savings and reopen cost remain unmeasured. This addresses post-view retention and should not change the never-opened cold baseline.

alternative.operation: Public QWidget::backingStore()->resize(QSize(0,0)) while explicitly hidden, followed by guaranteed full invalidation on next show.
alternative.tradeoff: Narrower pixel-buffer intervention, but QXcbBackingStore::resize may recreate a hidden native QWindow if close already destroyed it. QWidget-owned backing-store mutation requires native repaint/resize testing. The public API documents resizing, not a cross-platform memory-release guarantee. Use explicit zero dimensions, not default invalid QSize().
alternative.status: source-supported Xcb path, product behavior unverified; second-choice probe

limits: No product/test/build/probe/process/UI/VM execution performed; only read-only shell source/JSON inspection and this artifact write.
Local Qt source is Qt6.4.2; receipt uses distro Qt6.4.2+dfsg-21.1build5. Source establishes available APIs and expected Xcb behavior, not exact patched-runtime or compositor acceptance.

SHM RSS is shared with Xorg: 8404992 RSS versus 4202496 PSS and zero private in this receipt. A future release must consider Xorg/compositor total memory and server pixmaps; summed RSS can double-count shared pages. No helper process is proposed.
No destruction of logical widgets, native-font/dialog/theme removal, new allocator policy, experiment authorization, measured improvement or 40MiB attainment is claimed.
